issue_context.title: 'show create table' statement‘s default value should take escape character into account, like '\'.
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)

```sql
create table test(a int primary key, b varchar(20) default '\\');
show create table test;
```

### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)

sql create statement’s default value takes escape character into account. 
```sql
CREATE TABLE `test` (
  `a` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  `b` varchar(20) DEFAULT '\\'
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_bin
```

### 3. What did you see instead (Required)
sql create statement‘s default value didn't take escape character into account.
```sql
CREATE TABLE `test` (
  `a` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  `b` varchar(20) DEFAULT '\'
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_bin
```

### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required)

5.7.25-TiDB-v5.2.1

make check linter and correct code format for show_test.go and commit again, please check. And for the "format_test.go", sure back quote will be better and display right.  but what i confusing is in the old test case, like `\n`, `\r` will be treated as '\' 'r' '\' 'n' seperately, the func "replace" will not be used at all, so if meet a char '\n', will not act like back quote test does.  Anyway, if sure the previous format_test.go testcase is right, so just ignore this file's change
